SPF is an email check that verifies whether a sending server is allowed to send email for a domain.
Spirit malware
A malware backdoor referenced in security reporting that gives attackers remote access to a device.
Spoofing technique
Spoofing is pretending to be someone or something trusted, such as an email sender, website, or device.
spyware malware
Spyware is malicious or intrusive software that secretly monitors a person’s device, messages, location, or activity.
SquareML product
SquareML is an AI platform referenced in security reporting.
SSH protocol
SSH is a secure way to remotely log in to and control another computer over a network.
SSH Backdoor technique
An SSH backdoor is an unauthorized way to remotely access a system using the Secure Shell protocol.
SSH backdoors technique
SSH backdoors are hidden ways for an attacker to remotely access a computer through the Secure Shell remote-login protocol.
SSH keys protocol
SSH keys are cryptographic login credentials used to securely access remote computers and services.
SSL protocol
A protocol once widely used to encrypt data between a device and a website, now mostly replaced by TLS.
SSL VPN protocol
SSL VPN is a type of remote access connection that uses SSL-based security to connect users to a private network.
stable concept
A stable release channel is the normal software update track intended for broad use after testing.
Stable Branches concept
Maintained versions of software that receive selected fixes while avoiding major feature changes.
also: stable branch, stable kernel trees, stable trees
Stable Linux Releases product
Older maintained Linux versions that prioritize reliability and receive selected security fixes.
also: stable releases, stable software, stable packages
stable versions concept
Stable versions are software releases considered ready for normal use rather than testing or experimentation.
StarkMeet tool
A fake videoconferencing application used as a lure to deliver malware.
Startup concept
Startup usually refers to programs or scripts configured to run automatically when a computer or user session starts.
State Emergency Service of Ukraine organization
A Ukrainian government agency responsible for emergency response, civil protection, and rescue services.
state-backed groups threat-actor
State-backed groups are hacking or influence groups that are supported, directed, or protected by a national government.
state-linked concept
State-linked describes activity believed to be connected to or supported by a national government.
State-sponsored concept
Describes activity supported, directed, or carried out by a government or its agencies.
steal information technique
Steal information means to take data without permission, often to sell it, leak it, or use it for further attacks.
Stolen concept
Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.
stolen credentials concept
Stolen credentials are usernames, passwords, or login tokens that attackers have obtained without permission.
stolen data concept
Stolen data is information taken without permission, often later sold, leaked, or used for extortion.
Stolen Funds concept
Money or other assets taken from their owner without permission.
stolen information concept
Stolen information is data taken without permission, such as personal details, business files, passwords, or financial records.
stolen personal information concept
Private details about a person that criminals obtain without permission and may use for fraud.
Storm-0940 threat-actor
A threat-actor group tracked by Microsoft in security reporting.
streaming boxes product
Streaming boxes are internet-connected devices that plug into TVs to run video apps and other media services.
Struggle malware
Struggle is a malware family, tool, or threat name referenced in security reporting.
Submission Packets concept
Collections of proposed changes, evidence, and notes prepared for another person to review and approve.
Superusers concept
Accounts with the highest level of permissions to manage a computer or application.
SuperValu organization
A supermarket retail brand operating stores in Ireland.
supply chain concept
A supply chain is the network of vendors, software, services, and processes an organization depends on to operate.
Supply Chain Compromises technique
Attacks that reach victims by tampering with a trusted supplier, software dependency, update, or distribution process.
Supply chain security concept
Supply chain security is the practice of protecting the outside software, vendors, services, and components an organization depends on.
support tickets concept
Support tickets are records of customer or employee requests for help that support teams track and resolve.
surveillance concept
The act of monitoring people or activities, often covertly, as part of espionage, law enforcement, or malware functions like keyloggers.
SUSE Linux Enterprise product
A commercial Linux operating system designed for business and server use.
suspicious activity concept
Suspicious activity is behavior that looks unusual or risky and may indicate fraud, hacking, or policy violations.
Suspicious Cyber Activity concept
Unusual computer or network behavior that may indicate an attack or unauthorized access.
sweden other
Sweden is a country in Northern Europe.
SYN protocol
A TCP packet flag used to begin the process of setting up a network connection.
also: retransmitted SYN
Synack organization
Synack is a cybersecurity company known for managed security testing and crowdsourced penetration testing services.
also: SYNACK for a retransmitted SYN
Synology organization
A technology company best known for network-attached storage devices and related software.
Synology NAS product
A network storage appliance made by Synology that lets multiple users store, share, and back up files from anywhere.
synthetic personas technique
Fake online identities, often created with invented names, photos, and backgrounds, that can be used to deceive people.
Synthient organization
Synthient is a cybersecurity company referenced in security reporting.
syria other
Syria is a country in the Middle East.
SysGoRAT malware
A Go-based remote-access Trojan that lets an attacker remotely control an infected computer.
system access concept
System access means the ability to log in to or use a computer, application, or network.
System App concept
A system app is an application installed with high-level permissions that let it perform powerful actions on a device.
System disruption concept
System disruption means intentionally or accidentally making computers, networks, or services slow, unreliable, or unavailable.
System logs concept
System logs are records created by computers or servers that show important events, errors, and activity.
System prompt concept
A system prompt is a hidden or high-priority instruction that tells an AI assistant how it should behave.
SYSTEM-level privileges concept
SYSTEM-level privileges are the highest local privileges on Windows, giving code very broad control over the computer.
Systems Offline concept
A protective response in which computer systems are disconnected or shut down to limit possible damage.
T1036 technique

t1566-002
T1566.002 is the MITRE ATT&CK technique for phishing that uses malicious links in messages.
taiwan other
Taiwan is a territory in East Asia that is often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving regional targeting or geopolitical activity.
Take Control product
Take Control is a remote access and support product used by IT teams to connect to customer devices.
takedown technique
A takedown is an action to disable, remove, or seize malicious online infrastructure such as domains, servers, or accounts.
Talos organization
Talos, also known as Cisco Talos, is Cisco's threat intelligence and security research organization.
tampering technique
Tampering means changing or interfering with data, software, or equipment without permission.
targeted spear phishing technique
A scam message tailored to a particular person or organization to trick them into revealing information or opening something harmful.
targeted-phishing technique
Targeted phishing is a phishing attack aimed at specific people or organizations using tailored messages to seem more convincing.
TCP protocol
TCP is a core internet protocol that reliably sends data between computers by establishing a connection.
TCP Stack concept
The part of an operating system that handles network communications using the TCP protocol.
tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() other
A Linux kernel function that creates a TCP connection socket after receiving an initial connection request.
teamviewer

Technical findings concept
Technical findings are the concrete details a researcher discovers, such as what was vulnerable, exposed, or misconfigured.
telecommunications concept
Telecommunications means the technology and industry for sending information over distance, such as phone calls, internet traffic, and data links.
telecommunications providers organization
Telecommunications providers are companies that run phone, mobile, internet, or data networks for customers.
telegram

Telerik Report Server product
Telerik Report Server is a product for creating, managing, and delivering business reports.

Temperature Settings concept
Controls that set how warm or cold a device or environment should be.
templates concept
Templates are reusable starting formats for documents, messages, code, or workflows.

A popular stablecoin cryptocurrency pegged to fiat currencies like the US dollar, often used in crypto trading and scams.
text messages concept
Short Message Service (SMS) messages, commonly used for two-factor authentication codes but susceptible to interception.

The Information is a technology-focused news publication that reports on companies, startups, and the tech industry.
Themis product
Themis is described in the article as an IRONSCALES platform capability that evaluated the message.
also: IRONSCALES agentic AI analyst
third-party concept
A third party is an outside person, company, or service that is involved but is not the main organization or customer.
Third-Party Compromise technique
Third-party compromise is a breach of a supplier, partner, or service provider that creates risk for another organization.
Third-party dependencies concept
Outside software components that a program relies on to work.
Third-party risk concept
Third-party risk is the danger that outside vendors, suppliers, or partners can create security or business problems for an organization.
third-party script compromise technique
A third-party script compromise happens when attackers tamper with code supplied by an outside service so it harms a site's users.
third-party services concept
Third-party services are outside companies or platforms an organization uses to help run its business or technology.
third-party vendor organization
A third-party vendor is an outside company that provides products or services to another organization.
third-party vendors organization
Third-party vendors are outside companies that provide products or services to an organization.
threat actor threat-actor
A threat actor is the person, group, or organization carrying out a cyberattack.
Threat actors concept
Threat actors are people or groups that carry out harmful activity against computers, websites, or organizations.
threat groups threat-actor
Groups of people or organizations believed to carry out cyberattacks.
Threat hunter concept
A threat hunter is a security professional who proactively searches for signs of attackers inside networks and systems.
threat hunting technique
Threat hunting is the proactive search for signs that attackers may already be inside a network or system.
threat intelligence concept
Threat intelligence is information collected and analyzed about possible or active cyber threats.
